methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $35M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Portal Biotech is a Series A-stage biotech company founded by Andy Heron and Giovanni Maglia that has raised $35M to date. The analysis relies on stage-progression methodology due to the absence of comparable public or private peer data in the biotech sector that would support revenue or EBITDA multiples.

The stage-progression method applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $35M total capital raised as a proxy for current value, yielding an implied valuation of $70M. This multiplier reflects typical dilution and value creation patterns observed in Series A-to-Series B progression within life sciences. No alternative triangulation methods were available given the absence of relevant public or private comps.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $60M to $80M, with $70M as the median point. This narrow band reflects reliance on a single methodology rather than convergence across multiple approaches. Key uncertainties include: the absence of peer benchmarking data to validate the 2.0x multiplier assumption; stage-specific burn rate and runway relative to Series B fundraising timelines; and clinical or regulatory milestone achievement. A more robust valuation would require either comparable company analysis or DCF analysis incorporating product development timelines and probability-adjusted cash flows.
